findings.fix: Add `method="post"` (and an appropriate `action`) to the form element.
findings.violation: Without an explicit method, the form defaults to a GET submission, which would place the password (and account number, membership number, etc.) into the URL - exposed in browser history, server logs, and referrer headers.

findings.evidence:
`

We will text you about delivery updates.

`
findings.fix: Give the paragraph an `id` and reference it from the input with `aria-describedby`.
findings.violation: This explanatory text sits visually near the phone field but is not programmatically associated with it, so screen reader users tabbing to the input won't hear the disclosure.

findings.fix: Remove the digit-only `pattern` (or relax it to allow `+`, spaces, hyphens, and parentheses).
findings.violation: Restricting a `tel` field to digits-only rejects legitimate phone formatting such as `+1 555-123-4567`, parentheses, or spaces that `type="tel"` is meant to accommodate.

findings.fix: Make the field optional (or remove it if this is a consumer signup), and change its type to `url`.
findings.violation: A required "Company website" field is out of place on a consumer account-signup form (full name, email, home address, phone) and will block individual customers who have no company site; it also uses `type="text"` instead of `type="url"`, losing built-in validation and the URL keyboard on mobile.

findings.fix: Add `pattern="[0-9]{8}"` and `maxlength="8"`, and move the format hint into persistent helper text instead of relying solely on the placeholder.
findings.violation: The 8-digit requirement is only communicated via placeholder text, which disappears once the user starts typing, and nothing actually enforces the 8-digit constraint.

findings.evidence: "Membership number (8 digits)" and "Account number" are both `required` on a form titled "Create your account"
findings.fix: Remove these fields from the signup form, or mark them optional/for-existing-customers-only.
findings.violation: A brand-new signup form cannot require a pre-existing membership number or account number, since a new customer won't have one yet - this will block legitimate new users from ever completing the form.

findings.fix: Increase `size` to at least 8-10 characters, or remove the attribute and size via CSS.
findings.violation: A visual width of 3 characters is too narrow for most real postal codes (e.g. US 5/9-digit ZIPs, UK "SW1A 1AA"), making the field look wrong and encouraging truncated-looking entry.

findings.fix: Collapse "Overnight"/"Next-day" into a single option, and move "International" to a separate shipping-destination control (or remove it from this list).
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" describe the same delivery speed and will confuse users about which to pick, and "International" is a destination type, not a shipping speed, mixing incompatible categories in one list.

findings.fix: Remove the duplicate field, or clearly differentiate its purpose (e.g. "Legal name, if different from above") and explain why both are needed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the user's name twice under different labels, which is redundant and may confuse users into thinking the two fields need different values.

findings.fix: Remove the inline font-size override so it matches other fields, and make organization name optional or remove it if this isn't a business account form.
findings.violation: The inline 13px font is smaller than the rest of the form's text, hurting readability/accessibility, and a required "Organization name" field is mismatched for what otherwise reads as an individual consumer signup.

findings.evidence: `<label ... style="display:inline-block;float:left;width:140px">Preferred contact time</label>` next to a free-text `type="text"` input
findings.fix: Replace the free-text input with a constrained control (e.g. a `<select>` of time ranges), and remove the inline float styling in favor of consistent layout/CSS.
findings.violation: The field gives users no guidance on expected format (e.g. "2-4pm" vs "14:00"), inviting inconsistent, unparseable data, and the label uses an ad hoc inline float/width style instead of the layout approach used elsewhere in the form.

findings.fix: Either wire the button to its intended behavior (e.g. expanding a details panel) or remove it from the form.
findings.location: `#viewdetails-btn`, between row-contacttime and the dob fieldset
findings.violation: This button has no associated handler or visible target in the document and interrupts the form's field flow right before the date-of-birth fieldset, suggesting dead or incomplete functionality.

findings.fix: Widen the year range to cover realistic customer ages (e.g. current year minus 100 through current year minus a minimum sign-up age).
findings.violation: This excludes anyone born before 1950 (older than ~76 in 2026) or after 2009 (younger than ~17 in 2026) from completing signup, which is an arbitrary and overly narrow range for a retail customer base.

findings.evidence: first options are `<option>1</option>`, `<option>January</option>`, `<option>1950</option>` with no "choose a value" placeholder, and all three are `required`
findings.fix: Add a disabled, selected placeholder option (e.g. "Select...") to each select so the required validation actually forces a deliberate choice.
findings.violation: Because each select is pre-populated with a valid-looking default (Jan 1, 1950), a user who never touches these controls will silently submit that fabricated birthdate, and the `required` attribute won't catch it since a value is already "selected."
